top_strength: Jack solved an availability problem instead of losing the lead to it — Garland was booked on her date, so he ran the job out of Dallas while keeping her Garland pricing, and told her exactly why: "we are Garland branch. I is actually full that day but we can kind of run out of Dallas." His pricing block was clean and complete on the mechanics: "we are $101 per mover. So I think we did two mover team which would be a $202 hourly rate," the $115 trip fee, the 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute proration all landed in one uninterrupted pass, and he closed with the strongest differentiator he used all call — "we actually allocate 2000 dollars for every single move" — contrasted against weight-based competitor coverage. He also inventoried the home room by room and pressure-tested the volume against her two 10x10 units rather than guessing.
coaching_note: The whole Save Your Ass section is missing, and on this call that is a direct cost to the customer and to estimate accuracy. He set up the logic and then never used it: "it's all based on time. So ultimately, you know with the less up there is and if we're able to get done faster than, than that's how much you pay for." That is the opening line of the prep speech, and it stopped there — no consolidating kids' toys or loose drawer items, no photos off the walls, no take-a-carload tip. She is moving into two side-by-side ground-floor 10x10s she can drive right up to, which is the single easiest scenario in the book for a customer carload to shave 30-45 minutes off a 7-hour billed day. Second, close the loop on the booking: he handed her a passive "respond to that email if you'd like to move forward" with no ask to lock a date today, and never used her name once after collecting it.
phone_presence_notes: Friendly and easy to talk to, and the customer ended genuinely pleased ("Thank you so much for going over all this with me"), but the warmth ran almost entirely through repeated filler acknowledgments — "Cool," "Gotcha," "Okay" — with no empathy statements, no humor, and her name never spoken back to her.
